findings.title: Stale direction used for non-pointer activation
findings.message: The trailing icon click handler captures `state` from syncNumberField and uses a stale snapshot of direction; also if e.MouseButton() is NoButton (keyboard activation) it reuses state.direction which was set by the last pointer press and may be stale, giving wrong direction. Also e.Pos() for a non-mouse event may be zero.
findings.suggestion: Reset direction to 1 after each activation, and compute direction from the event only when it is a pointer event.

findings.title: Stepper toggling relies on stale Maker closures
findings.message: Reverting from stepper to inline restores icons through SetLeadingIcon(icons.Remove, state.leading), but Maker plan entries added earlier (lead-icon Styler setting DisplayNone, trail-icon styler/handlers) only check r.node.NumberButtons dynamically. The OnFirst MouseDown handler is added once and remains. More importantly, the stepper is applied only on the first sync where buttons differ. Rebuilding on later changes depends on Update re-running Maker, which is untested for the transition and may leave stale styles.
findings.suggestion: Verify the Maker/Styler reruns on Update after switching modes, and add handler removal or a guard so the inline mode is fully restored.
